summary: Round 7. The round-6 blocker is resolved in the strongest available form and I verified it independently rather than accepting it. baselines/mutants.txt entry 3 is gone; the fifth assertion in LogKeysTest.aKeyTooSHORTToCarryTheGrammarIsRefusedRatherThanThrowing measures green unmutated (:sequencer:test 254/254, and the full ./gradlew test exits 0) and kills all three prefix-guard narrowings: trailing slash dropped and epoch segment dropped both fail ONLY that assertion, with StringIndexOutOfBoundsException Range [32, 31) out of bounds for length 37; the bare-component narrowing dies too, though AssertJ aborts at the pre-existing bins.delta assertion (Range [32, 4) length 10) so the fifth assertion's kill there is by construction. As a bonus one of round 4's three unargued survivors -- startsWith replaced by a length test -- is now dead by the same assertion (Range [32, 31), length 37). Both REMAINING mutants.txt entries measured surviving the whole suite and both arguments hold on inspection: contains(SUFFIX) cannot change the return value because keyFor regenerates a suffixed key, and cannot throw because a '.delta' match cannot straddle a logPrefix containing no '.'; the reversed equals is trivially equivalent. The file is coherent after the deletion -- header carries no count, footer is last. The rounds:M4.8b1 positive-control clause is accurate and I reproduced it: substituting the literal startsWith("bins/ctl/log/0/") gives 13 failures, 12 of them 'expected N but was 0' (real entries dropped from recovery) with CommitLogTest.twoEpochsWriteToDisjointPrefixesAndNeitherSeesTheOthersDeltas breaking on '[the epoch DOES see its own chain] expected 7 but was 0' while both cross-epoch assertions pass -- exactly the tell the entry names. No production file changed this round (ChainReplay and CommitLog predate the round-6 verdict), so no request-rate surface moved; the filter still only removes GETs and adds none, and nothing here scales with records, shards, partitions or indices. Four minors, none blocking: a false Long.parseUnsignedLong clause left in the backlog-done row while its two twins were corrected; an argued mutant that the entry's own text shows is killable; two round-4 survivors still outside the tree; and two now-dominated assertions in the new test.

findings.file: docs/internal/product/backlog-done.md (M4.8b1 row, the 'BOTH REVIEWERS INDEPENDENTLY MEASURED A SURVIVOR' paragraph)
findings.title: The Long.parseUnsignedLong claim was corrected in two places this commit and left false in the third, which is the durable one
findings.detail: The staged row says: 'The end-to-end tests pin the PARSE, not the CANONICALISATION -- every interloper they seed is refused one step earlier by `Long.parseUnsignedLong`, `ckpt/<hex>.delta` included, whose digits are not hex at all.' That is true of one of the three interlopers ChainReplayNonDeltaKeyTest seeds. `<logPrefix>ckpt/%016x.ckpt` ends in '.ckpt' and `<logPrefix>0000000000000001.delta.tmp` ends in '.tmp', so both are refused by `!key.endsWith(SUFFIX)` at LogKeys.java:69 and never reach the parse at line 75. Only `<logPrefix>ckpt/%016x.delta` reaches it. This is exactly the clause I recorded at R6-3, and the delta fixes it in LogKeysTest's class javadoc ('two at the suffix guard, one at Long.parseUnsignedLong' -- which I checked and is correct) after round 5 fixed it in rounds:M4.8b1 ('refused by an earlier guard'). backlog-done.md was edited in this same round and kept the false form. The correct wording therefore already exists verbatim twice in the same commit. Not requested under review.md rule `minors-land`: the conclusion the clause supports -- that the end-to-end tests left the round trip unconstrained -- is right either way, and rule 12's measured lesson is that a further round spent on prose finds defects in the fix rather than in the change. Record it in the commit body.
findings.failure_scenario: backlog-done.md is what a future session reads to learn why LogKeysTest exists. A session doing M4.8b2 reads that the ckpt fixture is stopped at Long.parseUnsignedLong, concludes the `endsWith(SUFFIX)` guard has no end-to-end fixture behind it, and either deletes the `.delta.tmp`/`.ckpt` interlopers as redundant with LogKeysTest or targets its next mutation round at the wrong guard. Both leave the suffix guard less constrained than the row claims it is.

findings.title: An argued-equivalent mutant whose killing test the entry itself writes out, one round after the commit chose kill-over-argue for the sibling guard
findings.detail: I measured this mutant and it does survive the full sequencer suite, and the argument as written is true: with a prefix containing no '.', a '.delta' match cannot start before logPrefix.length() (it would have to place a '.' inside logPrefix), so the slice stays ordered and the final `key.equals(keyFor(sequence))` fixes the return value. But the entry's own closing sentence hands over the killer: `new LogKeys("a.delta", 1)` with key `<logPrefix>x` returns false under the real code (endsWith fails) and throws StringIndexOutOfBoundsException under the mutant, because logPrefix.length() is 35 and key.length() - 6 is 30. That is one T0 assertion in the file this commit just added, in the same shape as the five it already carries. testing.md rule 9 says a survivor is killed OR argued, and rounds 5, 6 and 7 of this very commit all resolved the same shape -- a guard pinned against deletion but not against its operand -- by killing rather than arguing. Recording rather than requesting for the same reason as R7-1, and because I did not raise it in rounds 5 or 6 when the entry was unchanged.
findings.failure_scenario: A later change reorders isEntryKey -- say it slices before checking the suffix, or M4.8b2 introduces a chain prefix that contains a dot (a tenant name, a version stamp) -- and the guard is now the only thing keeping the slice ordered. Nothing in the suite fails, because the file argues rather than tests it, and recovery throws StringIndexOutOfBoundsException on a listed key instead of skipping it: the exact takeover-loop failure this task exists to remove.

findings.title: Two of round 4's three further survivors are still neither killed nor in the tree; the third is now dead. R6-4 restated with fresh measurement
findings.detail: Measured against the staged tree, each run individually over :sequencer:test. (1) Both guards replaced by one length test, `if (key.length() < logPrefix.length() + SUFFIX.length()) return false;` -- SURVIVES, 254/254 green. (2) `!key.startsWith(logPrefix)` replaced by `key.length() <= logPrefix.length()` -- now KILLED by the new fifth assertion, so this delta closed one third of R6-4 without claiming to. (3) The NumberFormatException catch replaced by `sequence = 0` -- SURVIVES, 254/254 green. Both survivors are genuinely equivalent on the observable and I traced why: in (1) the length test guarantees begin <= end so nothing throws, and `key.equals(keyFor(sequence))` still admits only a key starting with logPrefix and ending in SUFFIX; in (3) any digit string that made parseUnsignedLong throw cannot equal the 16 zeros that keyFor(0) regenerates. So neither is a test gap -- but testing.md rule 9 puts an equivalence argument in baselines/mutants.txt precisely so it survives the session, and .gitignore:12 ignores .harness/, so round 4's argument for these leaves the tree with nothing. Recording, not requesting: adding two more prose entries is what the last four rounds were spent on, and this commit's rounds: entry argues that case itself.
findings.failure_scenario: M0.14 lands check-mutants.sh with an 80% floor on changed code. It reports two survivors in LogKeys.isEntryKey that no staged file explains, so whoever is on shift re-derives the equivalence from scratch -- or, more likely under a red gate, writes a test that pins the current expression shape rather than the behaviour, which is the coverage theatre rule 11 forbids.

findings.title: The new fifth assertion strictly dominates the first and third, which round 3 treated as grounds for deletion
findings.detail: The fifth case is the log prefix with its trailing '/' replaced by '.delta'. It starts with every proper prefix of logPrefix and with the whole one not at all, so every prefix-guard mutation that admits `".delta"` (line 78) or `"bins.delta"` (line 88) admits it too, and it then slices substring(32, 31) and throws. I could not construct a mutation the earlier two kill and the fifth does not: neither reaches the slice under the unmutated guard, so they only ever bite under a prefix-guard mutant, and the fifth is admitted by strictly more of those. Round 3's test review dropped `isEntryKey("")` on exactly this ground -- 'strictly dominated ... kills no mutant of its own' -- so the same standard now applies to two survivors of that cull. Test-file content is the test-reviewer's surface and I raise it only because the precedent is this commit's own; keeping them as documentation of which narrowing each case names is a defensible answer, and under `minors-land` this should not be fixed.
findings.failure_scenario: No behaviour fails. The cost is that the next mutation round reads five assertions as five discriminations, mis-attributes a kill to line 88 the way round 6's entry mis-attributed one to the epoch segment, and writes another mutants.txt argument on the strength of it -- the failure mode this commit's rounds: entry has now recorded twice.
